The respondent/SLAO, Karnataka Housing Board, Bengaluru, has made this reference under Section 77(1) of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (hereinafter referred to as 'RFCTLA Act' for short) for apportionment of compensation amount.

sentences.text: .2. The brief facts of the case is that the land bearing Sy.No.37/49 measuring 0.03.08 guntas of Byalalu village, Tavarekere Hobli, Bangaluru South Taluka has been acquired for the purpose of construction of houses.
Preliminary notification was issued on 19.03.2011.
Final notification was published L.A.C. No. 175/2019 in the Gazette on 27.11.2012.
The award was passed on 02.09.2015.
The L.A.O. has fixed the compensation of Rs.9,37,941/-.

As the suit in O.S.No.585/2013 in respect of the said property is pending for adjudication before Prl. Senior Judge and CJM, Ramanagara, the Doddaveeraiah M V Alias Veeresh vs Slao, Karnataka Housing Board on 4 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133664997/

sentences.text: 3 L.A.O. has sent the reference to this Court and has deposited a sum of Rs. 9,37,941/-.
The said amount has been kept in F.D. in the Syndicate Bank, City Market branch, Bengaluru.
.3. After receipt of reference, this court issued notices to the claimants.
All the claimants have entered appearance through their counsels.
The claimant No. 1 has filed claim statement.

.4. Claimant No.1 - M.V. Doddaveeraiah @ Veeresh has filed claim statement stating that the respondent acquired the property bearing Sy. No. 37/49 measuring 0.03.08 guntas of Byalalu village and passed the award in case No. KHB/LAQ/5/2010-11 dated 02.09.2015.

Further stated that as there was objectors, who have filed objections for payment of the award L.A.C. No. 175/2019 amount to the claimant No.1, the respondent referred the matter to this Court and deposited the award amount of Rs.9,37,941/-.
Further the said property was owned and possessed by claimant No.1 at the time of acquisition of land.

Further the said acquired property has been purchased by claimant No.1 under the registered sale deed dated 06.03.2008 for valuable consideration from one Munihanumaiah and thereafter khatha has been changed in his name.

Further stated that originally the land in Sy. No. 37/49 was belonged to one Veerachannaiah @ Earachannaiah and after his death, the land in question mutated in the name of his son M.V. Channakeshava, in turn, he sold the said land to Munihanumaiah through registered sale deed dated 06.03.2008 and thereafter the said Munihanumaiah sold the said property in favour of claimant No.1.

Further stated that one Chikkamuniyaiah and others had filed a suit in O.S. No.585/2013 against Munihanumaiah and others including claimant No.1 before the Prl. Senior Civil Judge and CJM, Ramanagara L.A.C. No.
175/2019 for partition and separate possession in respect of the above referred acquired property.
Further stated that the above suit has been transferred to the Prl. Senior Civil Judge at Magadi and renumbered as O.S. No.702/2014 and the said suit was got dismissed as not pressed in view of the memo dated 27.09.2021 filed by the plaintiffs.
Hence, prays to release the award amount.

.5. The claimants 2, 3, 4(a) to (d) and 5 to 7 filed claim statement stating that they admitted and confirmed the claim statement filed by claimant No.1 and they have no objections to disburse the award amount with accrued interest to the claimant No.1.
Further stated that they have no claim in respect of the acquired land in Sy. No.37/49 measuring 0.03.08 guntas of land of Byalalu village.

Hence, they prayed to release the compensation amount in favour of claimant No.1.
L.A.C. No. 175/2019 .6.

The claimants 8 to 12 filed separate memo stating that they have no objection to disburse the award amount with interest in favour of claimant No.1.
.7.
In order to prove their case, the claimant No.1 is examined as PW.1.

The documents got marked as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.10.
.8.

On the basis of the above, the point for consideration is that:
"Whether the claimant No.1 proves that he is the absolute owner of the acquired property and entitled for the compensation?"

sentences.text:
Heard the arguments, perused the materials on record, on that basis my findings on the above point is in the affirmative for the following:
REASONS .10.

This is a reference made by the respondent to the Court under Section 77(1) of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

sentences.text:
The property involved in this case is the property bearing Sy.
L.A.C. No. 175/2019 No. 37/49 measuring 0.03.08 guntas of Byalalu village,
Tavarekere Hobli, Bangaluru South Taluka and the said property has been acquired in case No.KHB/LAQ/5/2010-11 dated 27.11.2012.
This reference is made in view of the pendency of case in respect of the property in Sy. No.37/49 and other properties.

Subsequent to the reference of this case to the Court, the Court issued notice to all the claimants or all the claimants who were objected the compensation in favour of khathedars before the LAO.
.11.
The claimants 2 to 12 filed separate statements and memos on various dates stating that they have no objection to give compensation to the claimant No.1.
Only the claimant No.1 filed claim statement as well as led evidence in support of his claim statement and examined as PW.1 and also got marked the documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.10.
Ex.P.1 is the sale deed dated 06.03.2008 executed in favour of claimant No.1 by one Munihanumaiah.
As per the said sale deed, item No.2 is the property bearing Sy. No.37/49 L.A.C. No. 175/2019 measuring 0.03  guntas of Byalalu village and that has been sold in favour of claimant No.1.

On the basis of the said sale deed, the property has been mutated in the name of claimant No.1 and also the document shows that claimant No.1 is the khathedar of the acquired property as on the date of acquisition and even prior to acquisition from the date of aforesaid sale deed.

Ex.P.7 is the order sheet in O.S.No.702/2014 on the file of Prl. Senior Civil Judge and CJM,
Ramanagara.
In view of pendency of the said suit, the LAO has referred the case to the Court and the award amount has been deposited to the Court.
As per the said order sheet Ex.P.7, the plaintiffs therein filed a memo on 27.09.2021 stating that they are not pressing the suit and hence the said suit in O.S.No.702/2014 has been dismissed.
In the said suit, the claimant No.1 is the defendant No.7.
As the said suit in O.S.No.702/2014 has been disposed off, now there is no other dispute pending between claimants.

Apart from that, on 30.07.2022 the claimants 2, 3, 4(a) to (d), 5 to 7 filed a statement stating that they are not claiming any compensation in respect of acquired property and they have no objections to pay the compensation in favour of claimant No.1.
Similarly, on 28.09.2022 the claimants 11 and 12 filed a memo stating that they are not claiming any right over the compensation amount deposited to the Court.

Similarly, on 19.11.2022 the claimant No.10 filed a memo stating that he has no objection to pay the compensation to the claimant No.1 and he is not claiming any right over the compensation amount deposited to the Court.

Similarly, on 28.02.2023 the claimant No.8 filed a memo stating that she has no objection to pay the compensation to the Doddaveeraiah M V Alias Veeresh vs Slao, Karnataka Housing Board on 4 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133664997/
5 claimant No.1 and she is not claiming any right over the compensation amount deposited to the Court.

sentences.text: As such, except claimant No.1, other claimants are not claiming any right over the acquired property.

In the case on hand, acquisition of property in Sy. No.37/49 measuring L.A.C. No.
175/2019 0.03.08 guntas of Byalalu village is not in dispute and also depositing of compensation amount is not in dispute.
Except claimant No.1, nobody is claiming right over the said property and compensation amount.
The suit pending before the Prl. Senior Civil Judge at Ramanagara Court disposed off, when the acquisition proceedings has been commenced.

Therefore, this Court is of the humble opinion that the claimant No.1 is an absolute owner of the acquired property and the documents also standing in the name of claimant No.1 even according to the materials placed by the respondent as well as claimant No.1.
As such, the claimant No.1 is entitled for compensation in view of the acquired property involved in this case as claimant No.1 is the absolute owner of the acquired property.
Hence, I answer point No.1 in the affirmative.

In the result I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER

The reference made by the respondent/SLAO under Section 77(1) of L.A.C.
No. 175/2019 the Right to Fair compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act 2013 in respect of claimant No.1 is hereby allowed.
